content:
Two years ago, when Apple launched the M4 Mac mini, teardown reports quickly brought good news: the internal SSD was not soldered onto the logic board. This allowed users to upgrade the storage capacity themselves, and we even demonstrated how to do it.

However, in the latest M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini updates, the storage chips appear to have been soldered back onto the logic board.

The new Mac mini's storage has reverted to a soldered design, which is a step backwards

Expand Mac mini noted in a blog post that the NAND chips are soldered onto the logic board, similar to the situation with the M1 and M2 versions of the Mac mini. In other words, the SSD module can no longer be removed.

Expand Mac mini sells storage upgrade modules for the M4 and M4 Pro versions of the Mac mini. However, they said that, based on the current situation, "the possibility of providing support for the M6 and M5 Pro seems unlikely."

Without a slot, there's no way to replace it, and there's very little we can do. In August this year, we said we would expand our coverage once we had tested the actual machines. Now the results are out, and they are not what we had hoped for. We will continue to look for a breakthrough, but the possibility of providing support for the M6 and M5 Pro seems unlikely. If anything changes, we will announce it here immediately.

For comparison, Expand Mac mini's 1TB SSD expansion module for the M4 Mac mini is priced at US$300. Apple charges US$500 to upgrade the M6 Mac mini from 256GB to 1TB. Expand Mac mini's 2TB module sells for US$420, while Apple's equivalent upgrade costs US$1,000.

As for the Mac Studio, Apple's repair guide still indicates that the SSD is of a removable design. However, no teardown reports have been seen so far to confirm this.

If you are using an M4 Mac mini and considering upgrading the storage, you can refer to the detailed tutorial produced by Jeff Benjamin from 9to5Mac.

Although this is not the same as upgrading the internal storage, Satechi has launched a clever accessory with a built-in SSD enclosure and additional ports, suitable for the M6 Mac mini.
